newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares ease, wait for Bank Handlowy price.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares ease, wait for Bank Handlowy price.

text.p: Polish shares eased after Wednesday's slight gain and analysts said the market would likely maintain its flat trend or fall slightly both on Friday and during the upcoming large public offering of Bank Handlowy.
The bank, whose public offering starts next week and is seen worth a total of about $1 billion, is due to announce the price bracket for the offering's tranches by Friday.

"A lot will depend on the pricing of Bank Handlowy. The pricing of that issue should...allow an appraisal of currently listed banks," said Ryszard Wojnowski, an analyst at Polish Investment Bank (PBI) brokerage.

Analysts were divided on whether the currency crisis in the neighbouring Czech Republic would affect Poland, noting that while some foreign investors differentiated little between the two countries, others might shift some share buying to Poland.

The main market's all-share WIG index eased 0.3 percent to 16,434.6 points and turnover was flat at 158.6 million zlotys ($49.6 million) on all three markets. Losers led gainers by 49 to 28 with 23 stocks flat.

Analysts said Poland's good macroeconomic environment, reflected by the finance minister's Wednesday statement that year-on-year inflation could fall below 13 percent in December from 15.3 percent in April, would prevent steep falls.
They said this summer's large public offering schedule in addition to Handlowy and parliamentary elections due in September would also likely dampen buying in coming weeks.
Analysts said Thursday's strong selling after price fixing and the 1.8-percent fall by the WIG 20 index in continuous trade signalled a possible fall on Friday.
